properties.name: PEARFIELD LAUNCH RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Pearfield Launch Ramp is a boat launch on Saline Bayou in Kisatchie National Forest near Goldonna, LA. This launch area is one of the access points for the Saline Bayou National Wild and Scenic River. This area is popular for canoeing, fishing, kayaking, and other water activities.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: The Saline Bayou Natural and Scenic River entry/exit points include Hwy 126 Launch Site, Cloud Crossing Recreation Area, Pearfield Launch Site, and Hwy 156 Launch Site.

properties.name: DOGWOOD CAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Primitive campground located on Hwy 117 near FH 59 (Longleaf Scenic Byway). The campground has restrooms, water, trash receptacles, and area for trailers/campers.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From the intersection of I-49 and Highway 6 (Natchitoches), drive west on Hwy 6 for 4 miles. Turn left (south) on Louisiana Hwy 117 and proceed 16 miles to FR 397. which is just before Forest Highway 59, Longleaf Trail Scenic Byway. Turn left on FR 397 and an immediate right into the campground.

properties.name: OLD LSU SITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.services: HISTORIC STRUCTURE/FEATURE | OFFICE/RANGER STATION | PICNIC TABLES
details.description: The Old LSU Site is the original site of the Louisiana State Seminary of Learning and Military Academy which was established in 1860. The Seminary is where Louisiana State University had its beginnings. Remnants of the buildings may be seen as visitors enjoy the quarter-mile walking trail which meanders through the site.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Day use only: open 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset
details.directions: From Pineville, drive north on Hwy 71 for 3.6 miles to 2500 Shreveport Hwy, Pineville, LA. The Old LSU Site is located on the east side of the road, across from the Veteran's Administration Hospital and next-door to the Kisatchie National Forest headquarters. Parking is available at the main gate and overflow parking is available at the Forest Service headquarters parking lot.

properties.name: TURPENTINE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: There are four separate wilderness trails that have three separate trailheads that are accessible from a vehicle. (Backbone Trail, Turpentine Hill, High-Ridge, and Caroline Dormon) The Backbone Trailhead is located at what is also the Caroline Dormon trailhead and is equipped with a parking area, restrooms, trash receptacles, and an information bulletin board. The other two are trailheads that have limited parking and are equipped with traveler forms and a drop box for filled out information forms for your trip.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From the intersection of I-49 and Highway 6 (Natchitoches), drive west on Hwy 6 for 7 miles. Turn left (south) on Louisiana Hwy 117 and proceed 16 miles to Forest Highway 59, Longleaf Trail Scenic Byway. Turn left (east) on FH 59 and go to FR 339 or FR 329 for trailheads.

details.description: Primitive camping area within the National Red Dirt Wildlife Management Preserve. Restrooms are available. This camp is a designated hunter camp and has OHV access to Standstone Trail.

properties.name: CORNEY LAKE REC AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: visitors to the south shore camping area can utilize the facilities which include paved roads, lantern posts, fire rings, restrooms, ample parking, and trash receptacles. Visitors to this area can also use single and group picnic facilities which include a covered group-use shelter, several single picnic tables, a park-like setting with grass, a fishing pier, restrooms, ample parking, and trash receptacles.

details.description: The Iatt Lake Observation Pier and Day Use Facility is a newly built addition to the recreational opportunities offered by the Catahoula Ranger District. Built in 2003 by members of the Forest Service and various cooperators, the Iatt Lake Observation Pier is a must see attraction. Day Use Area: Restroom, gravel parking, handicap accessible, canoe boat launch, picnic tables, and an awesome observation pier with interpretive signs. The best times to observe migratory birds would be in the spring and fall. There are, however, many bird species that live at Iatt Lake and in the surrounding forests all year long due to the mild climate and open forests and waterways of Louisiana. There are also many other species of wildlife including beaver that can often be observed from the Iatt Lake Observation Pier. Trash disposal available.

Kisatchie Bayou Campground is a primitive walk-in camping atmosphere with 17 walk-in sites and 1 drive-in site at the middle parking area. details.description: The Kincaid Lake West Boat Launch is a modern paved boat launch area inside the Kincaid Lake Recreation Complex on the Evangeline Unit in the Calcasieu Ranger District. Kincaid Lake, a 2,600 acre reservoir, provides the setting for this attractive development. Also at this facility is the Lakeshore Trail access which connects to the Wild Azalea Trail, the Lamotte Creek Trail, and the Wild Azalea Spur Trail. Trash disposal available. Paved extended parking spaces.
details.feeDescription:
Day Use:
$5 per vehicle per day
details.directions: From Alexandria, drive west on Louisiana Highway 28 for 13 miles to Louisiana Highway 121. Turn left (south) on LA 121 and go 1/2 mile to Valentine Lake Road (Forest Road 279) and turn left. Go five miles to Forest Road 205 and turn left. Go 2 miles to the boat launch road which is just before the entrance pay station to Kincaid Lake Recreation Area.

properties.name: LORAN OHV TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Claiborne Trails are located in the Old Camp Claiborne where over 500,000 troops trained for World War 2 and was the third largest city in Louisiana during those war years. The trails are available for ATV, motorcycle, and horse use. Hiking and biking are also allowed on the trail; however, they are primarily used for motorized and equestrian riders.
details.feeDescription:
Day Use:
$5 per vehicle per day
details.hours: Day use only: open 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset
details.directions: The Loran/Claiborne Camp is located off U.S. Highway 165. From Alexandria, take US Hwy 165 South through Woodworth for 14 miles to La Hwy 112. Turn right (west) on LA Hwy 112 and travel 2.6 miles to FS Road 258. Turn right (north) and travel 1.5 miles to the Loran Trailhead and Campground.

properties.name: LITTLE CYPRESS REC AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Little Cypress Recreation Complex features a 3-acre spring-fed pond surrounded by cypress & various hardwood forest and is encircled by the ¿¿-mile Ol'Sarge Interpretive Trail. Little Cypress is a small day use recreation area that offers picnicking, fishing, fully accessible Ol'Sarge Interpretive Trail, volleyball court, and a group picnic shelter.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Day use only: open 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset
details.directions: From Leesville, take U.S. Hwy 171 south 7 miles to LA Hwy 10, turn left and proceed 8.7 miles. Turn left on Forest Road 471 approximately 1 mile to Forest Road 471A.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: This recreation complex is located along the banks of the beautiful Saline Bayou Wild & Scenic River. Recreation opportunities consist of fishing, camping, boating, hiking, and picnicking. An abundance of wildlife can be observed.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From Goldonna, take La. Hwy. 156 2.5 miles east. Turn left (north) on La. Hwy. 1233 and go to Forest Road 513. Turn left (west) on 513 to the signed recreation area

properties.name: GUM SPRINGS REC AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Gum Springs Campground offers numerous recreation opportunities such as camping, picnicking, and hiking in a picturesque setting along US Hwy 84. Restrooms, fire rings, tent pads, and trash receptacles are available.
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $10 per night
details.hours: Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m.
details.directions: From Winnfield, drive 8 miles west on US Hwy. 84 to the recreation area junction, a signed location.

properties.name: BLUE HOLE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Blue Hole Recreation Complex is a compact area that has much to offer visitors. From a group-use picnic shelter, day-use picnic area in the grass along the shore of Blue Hole, to a loop trail with an wildlife viewing platform. Canoeing is also available but limited due to the size of the Blue Hole. Gravel parking and trash receptacles are available.
details.feeDescription:
Day Use:
Group Site: $35 - $75 per day, depending on group size
details.hours: Day use only: open 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset
details.directions: From Leesville, take U.S. Hwy 171 south 7 miles to LA Hwy 10, turn left and go straight, when LA Hwy 10 turns right, onto Forest Service Road 405 (Tank Road). Follow FR 405 to the signs to Blue Hole on the left.
